status: Focused qualification passes on all three distributions; complete candidate 18 RPM builds are running. No publication or diagnostic-policy change.

root_causes.pending_counts: stream.processJetStreamMsgWithBatch enqueues PubAck before sigq. signalConsumersLoop updates consumer.npc asynchronously; PubAck and ConsumerInfo do not order this worker. A FIFO marker under the stream publication lock observes completion without changing stored messages or real consumer state.
root_causes.ack_floor: Msg.Ack and connection Flush only order protocol parsing; the consumer ack worker runs independently. PartialPurge and WorkQueue tests now require the consumer acknowledgment reply before asserting the ack floor or NAK redelivery.
root_causes.batch_routes: Batch APIs were sent through random cluster ingress before account route interest reached it. Both affected fixtures now use the existing ordered account-route interest marker.
root_causes.slow_leaf: The fixture repeatedly wrote PING after its intentionally expired write deadline had closed the leaf. INFO also precedes temporary registration. The fixture now accepts a real TCP pair and waits for createLeafNode to return; CONNECT/PONG establishes connected state, and an expired deadline plus socket EOF/reset establishes slow-consumer closure.

coverage.signal_control: 0, 1, 5 and 100 messages: holding the actual consumer mutex demonstrates that PubAck arrives while its count is still zero. Completion produces the exact count; a second marker leaves counts and store sequences unchanged.
coverage.partial_purge: Retains all 30 state assertions, uses completed acknowledgments, and invokes the real expiry callback with aged pending timestamps instead of sleeping.
coverage.leaf_negative: Verify zero counted slow consumers before CONNECT and exactly one after CONNECT, with actual TCP I/O and closure in both cases.

excluded_trials: Matrix 1 could not mount a new file into the read-only source tree. Matrix 2 exposed INFO-before-registration in the added pre-CONNECT negative case. Matrix 3 showed PING before authentication is rejected. Matrix 4 fixes this with explicit TCP acceptance and the real createLeafNode completion; all three distributions pass. None of the failed trials is accepted as qualification.
